Let $A$ be a nonempty finite alphabet identified with $[m]$, and let $p$ be
a probability vector in the sense of
[[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]].
A finite-alphabet IID source consists of random elements
$X_i:(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\to A$, $i\ge1$, on one probability space,
which are independent and identically distributed in the sense of
[[def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables]] and have common law
$p$. For every $n\ge1$, the finite vector $X^n=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ then has
probability $\mathbb P(X^n=x^n)=p^n(x^n)$ for each $x^n\in A^n$, with $p^n$
as in [[def-finite-law-self-information-and-entropy]].

Let $A$ be a nonempty finite alphabet identified with $[m]$, and let $p$ be a
probability vector as in
[[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]]. Its support
is $A_+:=\{a\in A:p(a)>0\}$. On $A_+$ define self-information
$\imath_p(a):=-\ln p(a)$; set $\imath_p(a)=0$ when $p(a)=0$ only to make a
finite-valued function on all of $A$. Using the finite entropy $H(p)$ from
[[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]] and the
natural-logarithm/nats convention from
[[def-it-information-units-and-logarithm-base]], define the surprisal variance
$$V(p):=\sum_{a\in A_+}p(a)(\imath_p(a)-H(p))^2.$$
For $n\ge1$ and $x^n=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in A^n$, define the product law
$p^n(x^n):=\prod_{i=1}^np(x_i)$. On its support $A_+^n$, define block
self-information $\imath_{p^n}(x^n):=-\ln p^n(x^n)$. Logarithms use the
natural base, matching the entropy convention in
[[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]].

Write $\ln$ for the natural logarithm $\log$ of [[def-natural-logarithm]]. Unless a base is displayed, every information quantity on this page uses $\ln$ and is measured in **nats**. For a base $b>1$ and $t>0$, define
$$\log_b t:=\frac{\ln t}{\ln b}.$$
The denominator is positive: $b>1$, $\ln$ is strictly increasing, and $\ln 1=0$ by [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]. A base-$b$ entropy or divergence is obtained by replacing each $\ln$ in the finite formulas below by $\log_b$; use $0\log_b0:=0$ and assign $+\infty$ to a positive numerator over a zero denominator. The case $b=2$ measures **bits**; $b=e$ gives nats.

For a finite nonempty set identified with $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$, a **probability vector** is $p=(p_i)_{i=1}^k$ with $p_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i p_i=1$; it is the outcome-weight vector of a finite probability space ([[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]). Its Shannon entropy in natural units is
$$H(p):=-\sum_{i=1}^k p_i\ln p_i,$$
with $0\ln0:=0$. For probability vectors $p,q$ on the same set $[k]$, the relative entropy is
$$D(p\|q):=\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\ln(p_i/q_i),$$
with value $+\infty$ if $p_i>0=q_i$ for some $i$. A matrix $A\in[0,1]^{N\times m}$ is **row-stochastic** when each row sums to one. For a probability row vector $p$ on $[m]$ and a row vector $X\in[0,1]^m$, the dot product $pX^{\mathsf T}=\sum_{i=1}^m p_iX_i$ is the acceptance probability under distribution $p$.

These definitions use finite sets only; entropy is between $0$ and $\ln k$, as proved where needed below.

For the finite-alphabet IID source in
[[def-finite-alphabet-iid-source]], with one-letter law $p$ and block law
$p^n$ from [[def-finite-law-self-information-and-entropy]], let $X^n$ have
that law. Write $H(p)$ for the finite entropy in
[[def-qa-35-finite-probability-entropy-and-stochastic-matrices]]. On the
positive-probability support $A_+^n$, define normalized block information
density using the natural-log/nats convention from
[[def-it-information-units-and-logarithm-base]]
$$I_n(x^n):=-\frac1n\ln p^n(x^n).$$
For $\varepsilon>0$, its epsilon-typical set is
$$T_n(\varepsilon):=\{x^n\in A_+^n:|I_n(x^n)-H(p)|\le\varepsilon\}.$$
Sequences of zero probability are excluded, so the definition never takes a
logarithm of zero.

Let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ be random elements with the same measurable target $(E,\mathcal E)$. They are **identically distributed** if $\mathbb P(X_i\in B)=\mathbb P(X_j\in B)$ for all $i,j\in I$ and $B\in\mathcal E$, that is, their laws in [[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]] agree. They are **independent and identically distributed (IID)** if, in addition, the whole family is independent in [[def-independent-random-elements]]. Independence means mutual independence, not merely pairwise independence. No moment assumption is part of either definition. The empty family satisfies these universal conditions vacuously.

Let $(X_k)_{k\ge1}$ be IID square-integrable real random variables, with $\mu=\mathbb EX_1$ and $\sigma^2=\operatorname{Var}(X_1)$. For $S_n=\sum_{k=1}^nX_k$,
$$\mathbb E|S_n/n-\mu|^2=\sigma^2/n,$$
and $S_n/n\to\mu$ in $L^2$ and in probability. Also $\mathbb P(|S_n/n-\mu|\ge\varepsilon)\le\sigma^2/(n\varepsilon^2)$ for $\varepsilon>0$.

For real random variables $(X_n)$ and $X$ on one probability space, write
$X_n\to X$ **in probability** when, for every $\varepsilon>0$,
$$\mathbb P(|X_n-X|>\varepsilon)\longrightarrow0.$$
This is precisely [[def-convergence-in-measure]] for the probability measure.

derivations.claim: Applying the same finite-valued measurable surprisal function to every coordinate preserves the common law and mutual independence.
Finite summation gives surprisal mean H(p), variance V(p), and square integrability.
Almost surely the block information is the surprisal sample mean, so the IID weak law gives the quantitative tail bound and convergence.

$p$. For every $n\ge1$, the finite vector $X^n=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ then has
probability $\mathbb P(X^n=x^n)=p^n(x^n)$ for each $x^n\in A^n$, with $p^n$
as in [[def-finite-law-self-information-and-entropy]].

For a finite nonempty set identified with $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$, a **probability vector** is $p=(p_i)_{i=1}^k$ with $p_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i p_i=1$; it is the outcome-weight vector of a finite probability space ([[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]). Its Shannon entropy in natural units is
$$H(p):=-\sum_{i=1}^k p_i\ln p_i,$$
with $0\ln0:=0$. For probability vectors $p,q$ on the same set $[k]$, the relative entropy is
$$D(p\|q):=\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\ln(p_i/q_i),$$
with value $+\infty$ if $p_i>0=q_i$ for some $i$. A matrix $A\in[0,1]^{N\times m}$ is **row-stochastic** when each row sums to one. For a probability row vector $p$ on $[m]$ and a row vector $X\in[0,1]^m$, the dot product $pX^{\mathsf T}=\sum_{i=1}^m p_iX_i$ is the acceptance probability under distribution $p$.

These definitions use finite sets only; entropy is between $0$ and $\ln k$, as proved where needed below.

For a finite-alphabet IID source and $\varepsilon>0$, let
$T_n(\varepsilon)$ be its typical set and
$\delta_n:=\mathbb P(X^n\notin T_n(\varepsilon))$. Then
$$0\le\delta_n\le\frac{V(p)}{n\varepsilon^2},\qquad |T_n(\varepsilon)|\le e^{n(H(p)+\varepsilon)},\qquad |T_n(\varepsilon)|\ge(1-\delta_n)e^{n(H(p)-\varepsilon)}.$$
In particular $\delta_n\to0$.
